info.title: Frontal Workflows API
info.description:
REST surface of the workflows product (`domains/workflows`).

Four Hono services mount on the same `/v1/workflows/*` prefix and the public
gateway routes that prefix to this product, so they are one API from the
outside and are described by one document:

  * `workflows-engine`    — workflows, versions, variables, templates,
                            search, validate, import/export, input/output
                            schemas.
  * `workflows-execution` — executions, tasks, step reports, and the run
                            read surface (runs, events, steps, logs,
                            artifacts).
  * `workflows-approval`  — human approval gates on a paused execution.
  * `workflows-trigger`   — triggers, schedules, webhooks, cron utilities,
                            reconciliation, and the unauthenticated intake
                            endpoints.

`workflows-temporal-adapter` is deliberately absent: it is gRPC-only
service-to-service and exposes no REST surface. gRPC remains the
service-to-service transport for this product; this document covers only
the REST API.

## Authentication

Every route except `/v1/workflows/health` and the two `/v1/workflows/intake/*`
endpoints requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. In `jwt` auth mode
(`FRONTAL_AUTH_MODE=jwt`) the token is an HS256 JWT and its `tenant_id`
claim is authoritative. In `dev` mode any non-empty bearer token is
accepted and the tenant header is authoritative instead.

The intake endpoints authenticate by HMAC signature over the raw body
(Standard Webhooks headers, or a legacy `x-frontal-signature-256` /
`x-hub-signature-256` header), not by bearer token.

## Tenancy headers

NOTE: these servers do not yet speak the canonical `x-frontal-*` identity
vocabulary. `extractTenantContext()` in
`domains/workflows/packages/http/src/middleware.ts` reads `x-frontal-tenant-id`,
`x-user-id`, `x-environment-id` and `x-service-principal`; only the roles
header (`x-frontal-roles`) carries the canonical prefix, and no
organization header is read at all. The parameters below are documented
with the names the servers actually honour today so a generated client
works against them. Migrating them to `x-frontal-tenant-id`,
`x-frontal-organization-id`, `x-frontal-environment-id` and
`x-frontal-user-id` is a server change, and this document must be updated
in the same commit.

`x-frontal-roles` (comma-separated) is read as the caller's roles when
there are no JWT claims, and `x-service-principal` is recorded on the
resolved context. Neither is documented per-operation because no route in
this surface branches on them.

## Request bodies never carry identity

`withRequestScope()` strips `tenant_id`, `tenantId`, `created_by`,
`createdBy`, `updated_by` and `updatedBy` from every request body before it
reaches a service: those come from the authenticated caller. Sending them
is silently ignored, never honoured.

## Field casing

Responses are camelCase in the engine service and snake_case in the
execution, approval and trigger services — the engine maps its persistence
rows through explicit DTOs, while the other three return their stored rows
directly. The document reflects each service as it is rather than
normalising them. Engine request bodies additionally accept the snake_case
spellings of a fixed alias set (`actor_id`, `input_schema`,
`output_schema`, `page_size`, `page_token`, `template_id`, `tenant_id`,
`variable_id`, `variable_overrides`, `version_id`, `workflow_id`); those
are the spellings documented here.

This document is hand-written against the four `src/server/rest.ts` routers
under `domains/workflows/backend/`.

get.description:
Answers before authentication so orchestrator probes, which carry no
credentials, are not reported as unhealthy. All four services register
this path; whichever one receives the request names itself in
`service`.

post.description:
Creates a DRAFT workflow owned by the caller's tenant. `tenant_id` in
the body is ignored; the resolved tenant always wins.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Filter by workflow status. The literal string `0` is treated as
"no filter", matching the proto's unspecified enum value.

post.description:
Templates are not tenant-scoped: the service stores no tenant on a
template and every authenticated caller sees the same catalogue.

patch.description: Only the fields present in the body are changed.

200.description: Deleted. The body is an empty object.

post.summary: Create a workflow from a template
post.description:
Creates a workflow from the template's definition, plus a first version
when the definition is non-empty. `variable_overrides` are merged into
the spec's `vars` object.

The new workflow's tenant is taken from `actor.tenant_id`, defaulting
to `system` — NOT from the request's resolved tenancy. This route does
not read the tenant context at all.

201.description: The workflow created from the template.

post.description: Full-text and faceted search over the caller's workflows.

Structural validation only, performed in-process against the supplied
definition; nothing is read or written. An invalid definition still
answers 200 with `valid: false`.

Recreates a workflow, its versions, variables and schemas from a
previously exported payload, under the caller's tenant.

Serialises the workflow with every version, variable and schema into a
JSON string suitable for `POST /v1/workflows/import`. POST rather than
GET because it mirrors the RPC; it takes no request body.

patch.description: Only `name` and `description` are mutable through this route.

200.description: Deleted. The body is an empty object.

post.description:
Moves a DRAFT workflow to ACTIVE and leaves exactly one version active:
the one named by `version` (its human-facing version number, not a
version id), or the latest when omitted. Rejected with 400 if the
workflow is not DRAFT or has no versions.
Rejected with 400 if the workflow is already ARCHIVED.

Returns an ARCHIVED workflow to DRAFT. Rejected with 400 if it is in
any other status.

Stores a new immutable spec for the workflow. When `spec.steps` is an
array the spec is compiled into a plan and a checksum; otherwise the
version is stored with a null plan and an empty checksum.

patch.description:
Replaces the stored `spec`. The compiled plan and checksum are NOT
recompiled by this route; only `createVersion` compiles.

200.description: Deleted. The body is an empty object.

post.description:
Makes this version the workflow's single active version, deactivating
whichever was active before.

Identical in effect to `promoteVersion`: the named version becomes the
single active one. The two operations differ only in name and intent.

get.description: Unpaged. Secret variables are returned without their value.

patch.description:
Fields absent, or explicitly null, are left unchanged — a variable's
value cannot be cleared to null through this route.

200.description: Deleted. The body is an empty object.

get.description: `inputSchema` is null when no schema has been stored for the workflow.

put.description: An omitted `input_schema` stores an empty object.

get.description: `outputSchema` is null when no schema has been stored for the workflow.

put.description: An omitted `output_schema` stores an empty object.

post.description:
Resolves the workflow's active version (or the one named by
`version_id`), compiles its spec into a DAG, validates every step type
against the resource policy, and records a RUNNING execution.

Rejected with 400 when the workflow has no active version.

201.description: The started execution and its initial DAG state.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The literal string `0` is treated as "no filter".

get.description:
Returns the execution, its DAG state, and — when one has been built —
a progress projection. State comes from the in-process state machine
when the execution is live in this replica, and from the persisted
state table otherwise.

post.description: Only a RUNNING execution can be paused; anything else is a 400.
Only a PAUSED execution can be resumed; anything else is a 400.

Terminates the Temporal workflow (best effort) and records TERMINATED.
Rejected with 400 when the execution is already COMPLETED or
TERMINATED.

Rejected with 400 when the execution is already in a terminal status
(COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, TERMINATED).

Rebuilds the DAG state machine and returns the execution to RUNNING.
Only FAILED or CANCELLED executions can be retried.

get.description:
Tasks are the execution's step runs, newest-updated first. Paging is
cursor-based on the task id; `page_size` defaults to 50.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The literal string `0` is treated as "no filter".

get.description:
A task carries no tenant of its own; ownership is inherited from its
execution and a foreign task answers 404 rather than 403.

post.description:
Resets the step run to PENDING and increments its attempt. Requires the
task to be FAILED or CANCELLED and its execution to be FAILED, RUNNING
or PAUSED.

Rejected with 400 when the task is already COMPLETED, SKIPPED or
CANCELLED. Cancellation of the underlying Temporal workflow is best
effort.

Written by the executor (the Temporal activity in `packages/runtime`),
not by end users. Creates the step run if it does not exist yet, marks
it RUNNING, and records a timeline event and a log line.

The same operation is served over gRPC as
`executions.v1.ReportStepStarted`, which is what the Temporal adapter
actually calls.

Written by the executor. Maps the adapter's verdict onto a step run
status (`succeeded`→COMPLETED, `failed`→FAILED,
`retryable_error`→PENDING, `waiting`→RUNNING), records a timeline
event, writes the reported log lines plus one lifecycle line, and
stores any declared artifacts.

Artifacts missing `name` or `storage_key`, and logs missing `message`,
are skipped silently. The same operation is served over gRPC as
`executions.v1.ReportStepResult`.

get.description:
A run and an execution are the same object under two names; this is the
read-oriented projection of the execution tables.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The literal string `0` is treated as "no filter".

parameters.name: started_after
parameters.description: Parsed with `new Date(...)`; ISO-8601 is the safe spelling.

get.description: Returns the run with every one of its steps, unpaged.

`next_page_token` is always the empty string on this route: the
`event_type` filter is applied after the page is read, so a cursor
would not be well defined. Page with `before_id` instead.

parameters.name: event_type
parameters.description: Exact match, applied after the page is fetched.

parameters.name: before_id
parameters.description: Return events older than this event id.

get.description:
Cursor-based on `step_id`; `page_size` defaults to 50. The `status`
filter is applied before paging.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The literal string `0` is treated as "no filter".

get.description:
`next_cursor` is present only when the page came back exactly `limit`
long, and is the timestamp to pass as the next `before_timestamp`. The
`level` filter is applied after the page is read and is upper-cased
before comparison.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Compared case-insensitively against DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR.

get.description: Unpaged. Artifact bytes live elsewhere, keyed by `storage_key`.

post.description:
`created_by` is taken from the caller's resolved user id, never from
the body. `signal_name` is forced to `approvalDecision` when blank: the
execution workflow listens on one decision signal and routes by step.

parameters.name: approver
parameters.description: Restrict to approvals this principal is required to decide.

get.description: An approval owned by another tenant answers 404, never 403.

post.description:
Records this approver's decision. `approver_id` defaults to the
caller's resolved user id. Once every required approver has approved,
the approval reaches APPROVED and the paused execution is signalled;
a failed signal is logged and does not fail the request.

A JSON body is required, but it may be `{}`.

A single rejection resolves the approval. The execution is signalled
with a `rejected` decision so the waiting step is released.

`reason` defaults to `Cancelled by user`. A cancelled approval releases
its step as rejected, so the run does not sit waiting on a decision
that is never coming.

Unauthenticated by design: external systems hold a signing secret, not
a bearer token. The registered webhook is matched by request path
against each webhook's URL path, then the raw body is verified either
with Standard Webhooks headers (`webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`,
`webhook-signature`) or a legacy `x-frontal-signature-256` /
`x-hub-signature-256` HMAC-SHA256 header.

A body that is not valid JSON is accepted and wrapped as
`{ "raw": "<text>" }`. Answers 202 when accepted and 400 otherwise —
both with the same body shape, distinguished by `accepted`.

parameters.name: x-frontal-signature-256
parameters.description:
Legacy `sha256=<hex>` HMAC over the raw body. Used only when the
Standard Webhooks headers are absent.

schema.description:
The provider's payload, passed through untouched. `event` or
`event_type` names the event type; anything else defaults to
`default`.

202.description: The delivery was verified and recorded.

400.description:
No matching webhook, an invalid signature, or an unsupported event
type. `accepted` is false and `error` says which.

post.description:
Unauthenticated by design, like the webhook intake. Matches the event
against every EVENT-typed trigger for the event's own `tenant_id` and
records a delivery per match. Unmatched events answer 200 with an
empty `matchedTriggers`.

get.description: A trigger owned by another tenant answers 404, never 403.

patch.description:
A trigger's `type` and `workflow_id` are immutable; only the fields
below can be changed.

200.description: Deleted. The body is an empty object.

post.description:
Takes no request body. Rejected with 400 if the trigger is already
enabled.

Takes no request body. Rejected with 400 if the trigger is already
disabled.

post.summary: Fire a trigger once, for testing
post.description:
Starts a real execution of the trigger's workflow using `payload`, or
the trigger's stored input template when omitted. Rejected with 400 if
the trigger is disabled.

200.description: The started execution, as the execution service returned it.

201.description: The registered webhook, including its signing secret.

get.description:
A webhook owned by another tenant answers 404: the record carries the
shared signing secret, so reading one would be enough to forge its
deliveries.

patch.description: The signing secret cannot be changed through this route.

delete.description: Rejected with 400 while any trigger still references the webhook.

200.description: Deleted. The body is an empty object.

post.description:
Creates a delivery of event type `test` and marks it SUCCESS. Nothing
is sent over the network; this exercises the delivery record, not the
endpoint.

Makes every SCHEDULE-typed trigger and the schedule it names agree: the
trigger's `enabled` flag is the intent and the schedule's status
follows it. Takes no request body.

NOTE: the tenant to sweep comes from the `tenant_id` QUERY parameter,
not from the resolved tenancy, and is optional — omitting it sweeps
every tenant. The route reads at most 1000 triggers per sweep.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description:
Restrict the sweep to one tenant. Omitted, every tenant's triggers
are reconciled.

post.description:
Validates the cron expression, computes `next_run_at`, and bridges the
schedule to Temporal. A failed bridge is logged and leaves the schedule
created without a `temporal_schedule_id`.

get.description: A schedule owned by another tenant answers 404, never 403.

patch.description:
A changed `cron_expression` is validated and `next_run_at` is
recomputed. The workflow a schedule targets is immutable.

delete.description: Deletes the Temporal schedule (best effort) and then the record.

200.description: Deleted. The body is an empty object.

post.description: Only an ACTIVE schedule can be paused; anything else is a 400.
Takes no request body. Only a PAUSED schedule can be resumed.

Starts a real execution out of band with the cron, then advances
`next_run_at` from the moment the schedule was due. Takes no request
body. Rejected with 400 for a DELETED schedule; a failed execution
start is a 500.

200.description: The schedule with its updated timestamps, and the run started.

post.description:
Pure computation against a UTC clock; nothing is read or written. An
invalid expression still answers 200, with `valid: false` and `error`
set.

200.description: The parse result with the next occurrences.

post.description: The same parse with no occurrences computed, reduced to a verdict.

bearerAuth.description:
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. In `jwt` mode the token is an HS256
JWT whose `sub`, `tenant_id` and `roles` claims establish the caller;
in `dev` mode any non-empty token is accepted and identity comes from
the headers instead.

TenantId.name: x-frontal-tenant-id
TenantId.description:
Tenant the request is confined to.

This is the header the servers read today. The canonical platform name
is `x-frontal-tenant-id` and these services have not been migrated to
it yet.

In `dev` auth mode the header is authoritative and an absent value
resolves to the tenant `system`. In `jwt` mode the signed `tenant_id`
claim wins and a header naming a different tenant is rejected with 403.

UserId.name: x-frontal-user-id
UserId.description:
The acting user, used for the audit fields (`created_by`,
`updated_by`, an approval's default `approver_id`). Ignored in `jwt`
mode, where the `sub` claim wins; defaults to `system`. Canonical name:
`x-frontal-user-id`.

EnvironmentId.name: x-environment-id
EnvironmentId.description:
Environment the request is scoped to. Recorded on the resolved tenant
context; no route in this surface branches on it. Canonical name:
`x-frontal-environment-id`.

PageToken.name: page_token
PageToken.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's next-page token.

TaskId.name: taskId
TaskId.description: The step run's own id, not its step id.

StepId.name: stepId
StepId.description: The step's id within the workflow spec.

RunId.name: runId
RunId.description: The execution's id — a run and an execution are one object.

InvalidArgument.description:
The request body was not valid JSON, or a service rejected the
arguments. `error.code` is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` or `FAILED_PRECONDITION`.

Unauthenticated.description:
The `Authorization` header was missing, malformed, or carried an
invalid token. `error.code` is `UNAUTHENTICATED`.

PermissionDenied.description:
The caller may not act on this resource — including a tenant header
that contradicts the authenticated tenant. `error.code` is
`PERMISSION_DENIED`.

NotFound.description:
No such resource for this tenancy. A resource owned by another tenant
is reported as not-found rather than forbidden so ids cannot be probed.
`error.code` is `NOT_FOUND`.

ErrorBody.description:
The JSON body returned for every failure across all four services,
produced by `toHttpErrorResponse` in
`domains/workflows/packages/core`.

message.description:
Human-readable description. For a non-domain error with a 5xx
status this is always the literal `Internal server error`.

metadata.description: Present only when the error carried metadata.

ErrorCode.description:
The canonical error vocabulary. HTTP status follows from it:
INVALID_ARGUMENT and FAILED_PRECONDITION → 400, UNAUTHENTICATED → 401,
PERMISSION_DENIED → 403, NOT_FOUND → 404, ALREADY_EXISTS and ABORTED →
409, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED → 429, INTERNAL → 500, UNAVAILABLE → 503.

Empty.description: An empty object. Returned by every delete route.

service.description:
Which of the four services answered: `engine`, `execution`,
`approval` or `trigger`.

Actor.description:
Who the caller attributes the change to. Recorded in the audit fields
when present; `system` otherwise. `actorId` is accepted as an alias for
`actor_id`.

tenant_id.description:
Read only by `instantiateTemplate`, which uses it as the new
workflow's tenant. Ignored everywhere else.

ActorRequest.description: A body carrying nothing but the acting principal.

nextPageToken.description: Empty string when there is no further page.

description.description: Stored as the empty string when omitted.

UpdateWorkflowRequest.description: Fields omitted, or explicitly null, are left unchanged.

version.description:
The version NUMBER to activate, not a version id. Defaults to the
workflow's latest version.

spec.description:
The authored workflow spec, with `${...}` expressions normalised.
Free-form; user keys are passed through untouched.

compiledPlan.description:
The compiled DAG. Absent when the version was stored without a
`steps` array.

checksum.description: Empty string when the spec was not compiled.

spec.description:
The workflow spec. When `steps` is an array it is compiled into a
plan; each step is read for `id`, `type`, `name`, `depends_on`,
`if_expression`, `config`, `on_true`, `on_false`, `on_ok`,
`on_abstained`, `on_failed`, `on_approve` and `on_deny`.

value.description:
Any JSON value. Omitted entirely when `secret` is true — a secret
variable's value is never read back.
Any JSON value. Stored as null when omitted.

UpdateVariableRequest.description: Fields omitted, or explicitly null, are left unchanged.

inputSchema.description: Null when no schema has been stored.

input_schema.description:
The JSON Schema for the workflow's input. Stores an empty object
when omitted. `inputSchema` is accepted as an alias.

output_schema.description:
The JSON Schema for the workflow's output. Stores an empty object
when omitted. `outputSchema` is accepted as an alias.

definition.description: The workflow spec this template instantiates.

UpdateTemplateRequest.description: Fields omitted, or explicitly null, are left unchanged.

slug.description:
Derived from `name` (lower-cased, non-alphanumerics collapsed to
hyphens) when omitted.

variable_overrides.description:
Merged into the instantiated spec's `vars` object.
`variableOverrides` is accepted as an alias.

status.description: The literal string `0` is treated as "no filter".

definition.description:
The workflow definition to check. `name`, `slug` and a `steps`
array are required of it; each step needs an `id` and a `type`, ids
must be unique, and every `depends_on` must name a step in the same
definition.

workflow_id.description: Accepted and currently unused by the validator.

payload.description: The exported document, as a JSON string.

The workflow, its versions, variables and schemas, as pretty-printed
JSON.

ExecutionActor.description:
Who the caller attributes the action to, in the execution service's
snake_case spelling.

tenant_id.description: Stripped from the body before the service sees it.

version_id.description:
Defaults to the workflow's active version. When neither is
available the request is rejected with 400.

status.description:
The state machine's status immediately after START_EXECUTION,
which is not necessarily the persisted `RUNNING`.

input.description: Echoed back only when it was supplied.
Absent when the execution was started without input.

output.description: Absent until the execution produces output.

state.description:
Step ids bucketed by DAG state. Every bucket is present, empty when
no state has been recorded yet.

projection.description: Present only when a projection has been built.

ExecutionStatusResponse.description: What every execution control route answers with.

ExecutionActorRequest.description:
Optional. A malformed or absent body is treated as `{}` rather than
rejected.

ExecutionReasonRequest.description:
Optional. A malformed or absent body is treated as `{}` rather than
rejected.

reason.description:
Recorded as the execution's error message and forwarded to
Temporal. Defaults to `User initiated termination` /
`User initiated cancellation`.

RetryExecutionRequest.description: Optional; a malformed or absent body is treated as `{}`.

retry_failed_only.description:
Recorded on the retry timeline event. The state machine is rebuilt
from the compiled plan either way.

Task.description: One step run of an execution.

type.description:
Always the literal `unknown`: the step's type is not stored on the
step run.

input.description: Absent when the step run has no stored input.

output.description: Absent when the step run has no stored output.

error_message.description:
`error.message` when it is a string, and the empty string
otherwise.

next_page_token.description:
The last task id of a full page, and the empty string when the page
was short.

RetryTaskRequest.description: Optional; a malformed or absent body is treated as `{}`.

CancelTaskRequest.description: Optional; a malformed or absent body is treated as `{}`.

ReportStepStartedRequest.description: Optional; a malformed or absent body is treated as `{}`.

attempt.description: Sets the step run's attempt when supplied.

ReportStepResultRequest.description:
The body is optional at the transport, but `status` is required by the
service: an absent or unrecognised verdict is a 400.

error.description:
A string `message` on this object becomes the step's error message
and is appended to the lifecycle log line.

duration_ms.description: Recorded on the timeline event and the lifecycle log line.

level.description: Upper-cased; anything outside the set falls back to INFO.

artifacts.description: Entries without a `name` or a `storage_key` are skipped.

Run.description:
A run is an execution projected into the run surface's shape;
`run_id` and `execution_id` are always the same value.

duration_seconds.description:
Elapsed time to completion, or to now for a run still in flight.
Zero when the run has not started.

step_index.description:
The step's position in creation order, computed on read rather than
stored.

latency_ms.description: Null until the step starts; measured to now while running.

event_type.description:
Free-form. The values this service writes are EXECUTION_STARTED,
EXECUTION_PAUSED, EXECUTION_RESUMED, EXECUTION_TERMINATED,
EXECUTION_CANCELLED, EXECUTION_RETRIED, STEP_STARTED,
STEP_COMPLETED, STEP_FAILED, STEP_RETRIED, STEP_WAITING,
TASK_RETRIED, TASK_CANCELLED and ARTIFACT_UPLOADED.

next_page_token.description: Always the empty string on this route.

next_cursor.description:
Present only when the page came back exactly `limit` long. Pass it
as the next `before_timestamp`.

storage_key.description: Where the bytes live; this service stores only the reference.

Approval.description: The stored approval row, returned verbatim by every approval route.

step_id.description: The step this approval gates; the decision is routed by it.

signal_name.description:
The workflow signal the decision is delivered on. Always
`approvalDecision` unless a non-empty `signal_name` was supplied at
creation.

ListApprovalsResponse.description:
The repository's page shape, returned unwrapped. `nextPageToken` and
`totalCount` are camelCase here while the rows themselves are
snake_case; that is what the service returns.

required_approvers.description: Rejected with 400 when absent or empty.

signal_name.description:
Falls back to `approvalDecision` when blank; an arbitrary name
would be signalled into a handler that does not exist.

expires_at.description:
ISO-8601. A background sweep cancels the approval with the reason
`Expired` once it passes.

ApprovalDecisionRequest.description: A JSON body is required, but every field in it is optional.

approver_id.description: Defaults to the caller's resolved user id.

CancelApprovalRequest.description: A JSON body is required, but every field in it is optional.

Trigger.description: The stored trigger row, returned verbatim.

event_filter_jsonb.description:
Matched against inbound platform events. `source` and `event_type`
are compared for equality, and every key in `payload_filter` must
equal the same key in the event payload.

UpdateTriggerRequest.description: Only the fields present are changed.

TestPayloadRequest.description: Optional; a malformed or absent body is treated as `{}`.

execution.description:
The execution service's `startExecution` response, passed through
unchanged.

Webhook.description:
The stored webhook row, returned verbatim — including `secret`, the
shared HMAC signing key.

url.description:
The registered endpoint. Its path is what inbound intake requests
are matched against.

secret.description: The signing secret. Returned in full on every read.

events.description: Accepted event types. An empty list accepts every event type.

secret.description: The HMAC signing secret inbound deliveries are verified with.

events.description: Defaults to the empty list, which accepts every event type.

UpdateWebhookRequest.description: Only the fields present are changed; `secret` is not mutable.

Delivery.description: The stored delivery row, returned verbatim.

Schedule.description: The stored schedule row, returned verbatim.

temporal_schedule_id.description: Null when the Temporal bridge failed at creation.

timezone.description:
Stored as given, defaulting to `UTC`. Cron evaluation itself is
always done in UTC.

cron_expression.description: Rejected with 400 when it does not parse.

input.description: The input document each scheduled run is started with.

UpdateScheduleRequest.description: Only the fields present are changed.

PauseScheduleRequest.description: Optional; a malformed or absent body is treated as `{}`.

count.description: How many upcoming occurrences to compute.

description.description:
A best-effort English rendering, present only when the expression
parsed. Falls back to `Custom schedule`.

isRecurring.description: True when more than one upcoming occurrence was computed.

webhookId.description: Empty string when no registered webhook matched the path.

deliveryId.description: Present only when the delivery was recorded.

triggerIds.description: The triggers bound to the matched webhook.

tenant_id.description:
The tenant whose triggers are matched. This endpoint is
unauthenticated, so the tenancy comes from the event body here and
not from a header.
